axes.name: area
axes.purpose: Where the work lands. Decides who reads the issue and which docs it draws intent from.

axes.name: kind
axes.purpose: What sort of work it is. Decides the route: spec loop, a plain pull request, or a throwaway probe.

axes.name: flow
axes.purpose: Where the issue sits in the queue. A statement about the ticket, never about the work.

labels.name: gameplay
labels.description: Rules and mechanics of the simulation
labels.when: The change alters what the game does: a week, a contest, a contract, an incident, a trait. Not the numbers inside a rule that already exists — those are `balance`.

labels.name: balance
labels.description: Numbers, baseline and the simulation harness
labels.when: The rule stays, the numbers move: salaries, prize money, recovery rates, thresholds, stat weights. Also the harness that measures them and the baseline it compares against.

labels.name: game-tech
labels.description: Shell, scene, art, animation, sound, localization
labels.when: Everything between the core and the player: the Vite shell, the Pixi scene, DOM panels, sprite pipeline, audio, saves, the localization mechanism.

labels.name: harness
labels.description: Process, gates, CI, the agent loop
labels.when: The repository's own machinery: `pnpm verify`, hooks, permissions, templates, CI workflows, the spec loop, anything that changes how work gets done rather than what the game does.

labels.name: content
labels.description: Data under content/, no code change
labels.when: Writing events, traits, disciplines, regions, name pools against an existing schema. If the schema itself has to change, the area is `gameplay` and this is not enough.

labels.name: mechanic
labels.description: Goes through the spec loop: two pull requests (ADR 0009)
labels.when: Adds or changes behaviour the specs have to record. Proposal first, code second, `openspec archive` on the implementation branch.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Behaviour differs from the spec that records it
labels.when: The rule is already written down and the code disagrees with it. Branch type `bugfix`, or `hotfix` when it is on master. If no spec says what the behaviour should be, it is not a bug yet — it is a `mechanic`.

labels.name: tooling
labels.when: Something under `tools/`, a package script, a CI job. No spec delta, one pull request.

labels.name: adr
labels.description: A decision, its own pull request before any spec
labels.when: A question of the form 'why this way and not another' whose answer outlives the change. ADRs are never rewritten, so they land alone and first.

labels.name: spike
labels.description: Answers a question; the code is throwaway
labels.when: The deliverable is a finding, not a feature. Anything built is labelled throwaway in the report and is not merged as-is.

labels.name: docs
labels.when: `docs/`, `README`, digests. Note that `docs/design/*` is the intent layer and changes only on the author's explicit request.

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: Has an open dependency; the blocker is named in the body
labels.when: Put it on when the dependency is opened and take it off when the dependency merges. A blocker stated only in prose goes stale unnoticed — that is what this label is for.

labels.name: tracking
labels.description: Holds a checklist of other issues; not worked on itself
labels.when: A group that is not yet specified far enough for real issues. Items without a number are deliberately unwritten, and that is visible.
